newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to assess aircraft makers proposals -- PM.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to assess aircraft makers proposals -- PM.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Wednesday Turkey would assess proposals by McDonnell Douglas Corp, Airbus Industrie and Lockheed Martin Corp on aircraft production.

"We attach great importance to all the proposals brought to us relating to cooperation with the companies Airbus, McDonnell and Lockheed," Erbakan said in comments to reporters before meeting McDonnell Douglas Corp chairman John McDonnell.
"These proposals will be analysed by us and the solution producing the most benefit for the sides in cooperation will be put forward," he said.
Last month, Erbakan said Turkey was planning to buy 50 civil aircraft worth a total $4 billion under an offset agreement.
At the time he said the government had held talks with senior officials from Airbus. Under the planned offset accord Turkey would manufacture half of the parts for the civil aircraft, he said.
Erbakan said on Wednesday Turkey was seeking an agreement with the maximum possible level of Turkish parts supply and complete know-how cooperation.
